newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Bottom-picking in tech stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Bottom-picking in tech stocks.

text.p: Call options in some battered technology stocks were drawing interest again after Monday's dramatic market reversal and today's Federal Reserve credit tightening, which was as expected, traders said.
"It's safe to say that some of them were trying to do some bottom-fishing in the tech stocks," said Rod Jamieson, vice president of option strategies at EVEREN Securities.

"I think people saw last night's reversal as a reversal day and they're looking at a little bounce -- and they're getting it in some of them," he added. Tech stocks held on to gains today despite a downturn in the choppy overall market.
Iomega Corp's April 15.0 call on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) was the most actively traded option overall, with 6,809 contracts changing hands by late trade. The stock was up 2-5/8 at 16-3/4.

Cascade Communications' April 25.0 call was the heaviest traded option at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, with 4,076 contracts traded. The deep out-of-the-money July 40.0 call also traded 2,513 contracts. The stock was up 2-1/16 at 26-7/8.
Cisco Systems Inc's April 50.0 call also had volume of 2,495 as the stock rose 3/4 to 47-7/8.
International Business Machines Corp and Intel Corp also saw some good call buying.

Traders said the market was generally growing optimistic about a resumption of its uptrend, with interest-rate worries out of the way at least for now. But they expected the market to stay choppy, given the wild swings after news of a quarter-point rate hike by the Federal Reserve today.
Jamieson said the market flipped back and forth so fast that many put buyers chasing down-moves and call buyers chasing up-moves never got their orders filled -- and avoided getting hurt as a result.
Bill Yates at DYR Associates said today's flip-flop probably would not make much difference beyond this week and noted that it could be a good time to look for bargains.

But he noted that buying the stock and selling out-of-the-money calls -- a buy-write -- would work better than buying calls outright. Even though the stock would get called away if it rallies too much, the position benefits from time decay and the plump premium on the calls would provide a cushion for the stock's downside.
"When a stock drops and implied volatility increases, the thing to do is buy that stock and sell volatility," he said.

"The ones that we're particularly looking at now -- because they've held implied volatility and they've also taken a number of hits -- are networking stocks," he added, noting that he liked 3Com Corp and perhaps Cisco.
Elsewhere, Jay Shartsis, director of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co, said higher than usual levels of activity in out-of-the-money calls of Coventry Corp and Galoob Toys Inc were interesting.
While volume was not extraordinary, the firms were both subject to occasional takeover rumors, he said. Coventry stock gained 1-3/4 to 12-1/8 and Galoob rose 3/8 to 17.
